newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian Insurance has 18 mln kroon 8-month profit.
newsitem.headline: Estonian Insurance has 18 mln kroon 8-month profit.

text.p: Estonian Insurance, the one-time state insurer that was recently sold to one of the Baltic state's top banks, Savings Bank, said Monday it made profits of 18 million kroons in the first eight months of 1996.
This compared with a loss for the whole of last year of 1.8 million kroons, Estonian Insurance general manager Ivar Virkus told Reuters.
He also said the firm was hoping to quote its shares.
"We are just now restructuring our company and at the end of next year Estonian Insurance will aim for the stock exchange," he said.
Newspaper Aripaev said Estonian Insurance was considering issuing some 10 percent of its stock, although the plans were at the very preliminary stage.
Savings Bank bought Estonian Insurance, the largest insurer in the country, for 32.2 million kroons. It has 60 percent of the non-life insurance market and 21 percent of the life market.
Virkus said the company's gross premiums over the first eight months were 123 million kroons.
He added the non-life market was usually the most profitable sector for the company but that in August life insurance for the first time showed a 2.0 million kroon profit.
